topicName: Handling Unstructured and Semi-Structured Data (JSON, XML, Parquet, Avro)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Handling Unstructured and Semi-Structured Data in ETL"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Modern data engineering pipelines frequently ingest data that does not conform to traditional relational schemas. This tutorial covers strategies, formats, and code patterns for processing JSON, XML, Parquet, and Avro within an ETL architecture."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Understanding Data Formats"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"JSON (JavaScript Object Notation): Highly readable, semi-structured, widely used in APIs and web event streaming. Best handled by parsing nested dictionaries."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"XML (Extensible Markup Language): Hierarchical data format common in legacy enterprise systems. Requires specialized parsers to flatten node trees."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Parquet: A columnar storage format optimized for analytical queries (OLAP). Excellent for compression and predicate pushdown in data lakes."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Avro: A row-based storage format featuring strict schema evolution capabilities, making it ideal for event streaming architectures like Kafka."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Processing JSON and XML with Python and Pandas"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"When building an ETL pipeline, you often need to flatten deeply nested JSON payloads into tabular formats for data warehouse ingestion."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"import pandas as pd
import json

# Sample nested JSON data
raw_data = [
    {"id": 1, "user": {"name": "Alice", "role": "Admin"}, "tags": ["etl", "python"]},
    {"id": 2, "user": {"name": "Bob", "role": "User"}, "tags": ["data", "sql"]}
]

# Normalize nested JSON structure
df = pd.json_normalize(
    raw_data,
    record_path=['tags'],
    meta=['id', ['user', 'name'], ['user', 'role']],
    record_prefix='tag_'
)
print(df.head())"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Working with Parquet and Avro in Apache Spark"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"For big data workloads, Apache Spark provides native support for reading and writing Parquet and Avro files efficiently while preserving schema integrity."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"from pyspark.sql import SparkSession

spark = SparkSession.builder \
    .appName("ETL Formats Tutorial") \
    .getOrCreate()

# Read JSON data with inferred schema
df_json = spark.read.option("multiline", "true").json("s3://my-bucket/data/input.json")

# Write data to Parquet format with Snappy compression
df_json.write \
    .mode("overwrite") \
    .option("compression", "snappy") \
    .parquet("s3://my-bucket/data/parquet_output/")

# Read Avro stream/files
df_avro = spark.read \
    .format("avro") \
    .load("s3://my-bucket/data/input.avro")

df_avro.printSchema()"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Best Practices for ETL Pipelines"},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Schema Enforcement: Always define explicit schemas when reading JSON or Avro to prevent downstream type coercion errors."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Partitioning: Store Parquet files using partition keys (such as year/month/day) to drastically reduce query scan costs."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Error Handling: Implement Dead Letter Queues (DLQ) to capture malformed JSON or XML records without failing the entire ETL batch."}]
